title: Linus Torvalds's 1991 Usenet Post That Started Linux
explainer: In August 1991, a Finnish student named Linus Torvalds posted to the comp.os.minix newsgroup that he was writing 'a (free) operating system (just a hobby, won't be big and professional)'. That hobby kernel, combined with existing free-software tools, grew into the Linux systems developers now run on servers, laptops, and inside nearly every container.

title: The GNU Project and Why Purists Say 'GNU/Linux' (1983)
explainer: Richard Stallman founded the GNU Project in 1983 to build a free, Unix-compatible operating system from scratch, and by the time Torvalds's kernel appeared in 1991, GNU had already produced most of the everyday command-line tools, the compiler, the shell, and core utilities, that a Linux system still runs today. The system you administer as 'Linux' is really a kernel wrapped in a large body of GNU tooling, which is the origin of the ongoing 'GNU/Linux' naming debate.
